verses.1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
verses.2: How long will you keep this up? How much longer will you spout such nonsense? Speak, and then we will respond.
verses.3: Why are we treated like dumb beasts in your eyes? Why must we be locked away like animals?
verses.4: The one who devours himself in his anger—will the land be abandoned on his account? Will a rock be uprooted from its place?
verses.5: The light of the wicked will go out, and the flame of their lamp will not continue.
verses.6: Their light becomes darkness in their dwelling, and their lamp is snuffed out over them.
verses.7: His own steps will entangle him, and his own counsel will fall on him.
verses.8: For he is caught in a net of his own making, and he walks on a snare he has set.
verses.9: He lays hold of his own feet in a trap, and the snares are strong above him.
verses.10: His rope is hidden in the earth, and his trap is upon the path.
verses.11: He is surrounded by sorrows, and he is scattered beneath his feet.
verses.12: He is hungry in his affliction, and a violent drought consumes his side.
verses.13: He devours the flesh of his own bones; death consumes his firstborn.
verses.14: He is torn from his tent by his trust, and the destroyer sets him in a wasteland.
verses.15: His dwelling becomes desolate, and no one sows on his field.
verses.16: From beneath his roots, they dry up; from above, his harvest is cut off.
verses.17: His memory is blotted out from the earth, and his name is not known outside.
verses.18: He is driven from light into darkness, and from the land he is uprooted.
verses.19: He has no son or heir among his people, nor any survivor in his generations.
verses.20: The last will groan over him, and the first will be seized with dread.
verses.21: These are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is a place where no one knows God.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 3: "treated like dumb beasts" reflects the Hebrew phrase "nechshavnu kabeema," which literally means "we are counted as beasts."  
- v. 17: "outside" is a contextual rendering of "penei chutz," which can mean "in the open" or "outside" in this context.  
- v. 19: "his generations" is a contextual translation of "mego'ro," which refers to descendants or lineage.  
- v. 21: "place where no one knows God" renders "mekom lo yada' el," which is a direct statement about a location devoid of divine knowledge or presence.
